title: kathy castor comments on prosecution changes affecting major florida fraud case
text:
Kathy Castor U.S. House of Representatives from Florida | Official U.S. House Headshot
Kathy Castor U.S. House of Representatives from Florida | Official U.S. House Headshot
U.S. Representative Kathy Castor, who has served in the U.S. Congress representing Florida's 14th District since 2007, recently shared updates on a significant legal case through her social media platform. Castor, born in Miami and currently residing in Tampa, is an alumna of Emory University and Florida State University.
On July 8, 2025, Rep. Castor tweeted about Gordon's leadership in prosecuting Leo Govoni, a St. Petersburg man accused of stealing over $100 million from medical trust funds intended for individuals with disabilities, injured workers, and retirees across Florida. The post can be viewed here.
Later that day at 22:00 UTC, Castor encouraged her followers to "Tune in! ," directing them to further information available through the link she provided here.
On July 9, 2025, she addressed the case again by describing Leo Govoni as a fraudster accused of orchestrating one of Florida’s largest fraud schemes in recent history. She expressed concern that the termination of the federal prosecutor might be an act of political retribution potentially jeopardizing justice for victims who have suffered extensively. The tweet can be accessed here.
Kathy Castor has been a prominent figure since replacing Jim Davis in Congress and has previously served in the Florida House of Representatives.
